heart: Make browser-local mutation boring: bounded admission before mutation, provider cancellation, same-origin coordination where available, inspectable mutation receipts, and honest storage non-claims.
riskiestIncompletePiece: OPFS posture was at risk of remaining advice/prose instead of an inspectable runtime receipt that callers and probes can assert.
changes: Added browserrt.browser-storage-posture-receipt.v1 in src/browser-storage-posture.mjs: quota estimate, internal byte ledger, persistence status/request, Web Locks/Buckets availability, last mutation receipt, admission status, and explicit quota/eviction/privacy non-claim proof flags.
Changed postured OPFS factories in src/browserrt.mjs to return postureReceipt and emit receipt/ledger trace fields instead of hiding posture evidence inside diagnostic prose.

Extended src/types.d.ts with RtBrowserStoragePostureReceipt plus a deduplicated RtBrowserStoragePostureConfig surface so caller-supplied internalByteLedger and lastMutationReceipt are typed once and reused.
Hardened tools/browser_storage_posture_probe.mjs and tools/browser_storage_posture_contract_audit.mjs to prove both estimate-only and supplied-ledger receipt paths.
Refactored/minified the posture module and type config to keep runtime-core closure and npm src-byte budgets under guard while adding receipt substance.
Compacted superseded linked datacube artifacts while preserving referenced paths, restoring the artifact budget.

auditRefactor.whatChanged: Refactored browser-storage posture into a compact receipt-producing module and deduplicated the TS posture config.
auditRefactor.whyItMatters: This added runtime-inspectable substance while respecting the project vice/risk: proof/code sprawl around a small runtime wedge.

nextRisks: Package src-byte budget now passes by one byte; the next change should either split heavy src surfaces from the shipped adoption wedge or intentionally raise/rejustify the budget after slimming elsewhere.
OPFS posture receipt still depends on caller-supplied internalByteLedger; the next behavioral slice should connect it to a real per-store byte ledger rather than a caller-provided summary.
Default root import is still compatibility-heavy; runtime-core remains the adoption escape hatch rather than the default path.
nonClaims: No runtime promotion, semver change, package publication, production readiness, cross-browser guarantee, browser quota reservation, eviction survival, fsync/power-loss durability, OPFS side-channel mitigation, Storage Buckets support, Service Worker lifetime guarantee, Web Lock fairness guarantee, automatic repair claim, or root-entry slimming claim.
The new receipt is a local posture/admission evidence shape; it does not make OPFS durable, persistent, private, globally fair, or quota-reserved.
